images.title: Equally strong walls
images.purpose: Shows that a 60 ft wall with 3 bags and a 40 ft wall with 2 bags both use one bag for every 20 ft.
images.composition: Two plain walls stacked one above the other, left aligned, each split into 20 ft sections with one cement bag under each section. Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text.
images.exact_structure: Top wall: a teal (#0072B2) brick strip 60 units long split by thin dark outline colour (#2B2B2B) lines into 3 equal sections, with one amber (#E69F00) cement bag under each section, label '60 ft, 3 bags' to its right. Bottom wall: a teal brick strip 40 units long split into 2 equal sections, one amber bag under each, label '40 ft, 2 bags' to its right. A thin bracket over the first section of the top wall carries the label '20 ft'. Under both walls, in reddish purple (#CC79A7), the label 'both 20 : 1'. Exactly 2 walls, 5 sections, 5 bags.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The walls are equally strong because each 20 ft gets one bag.
images.description: Shows that a 60 ft wall with 3 bags and a 40 ft wall with 2 bags both use one bag for every 20 ft.
images.teaching_notes: Walls drawn to scale (3 : 2 in length); no workers or tools.

image_decisions.why: Matching each 20 ft section to one bag shows why fewer bags can still mean the same strength.
